" Ars Poetica ", or " The Art of Poetry ", sometimes referred to as the "Epistula ad Pisones" , or "Epistle to the Pisos", is a poem written by Horace c. 19 BC, [ 1 ] in which he advises poets on the art of writing poetry and drama. The Ars Poetica has "exercised a great influence in later ages on European literature, notably on French drama", [ 2 ] and has inspired poets and authors since it was written. [ 3 ] Although it has been well-known since the Middle Ages , it has been used in literary criticism since the Renaissance . [ 4 ]
